acceptance_criteria.text: POST /api/bundles/ with filter_unread and filter_shared returns and persists those values on later GET /api/bundles/<id>/, and a bundle created without them returns "off" for both.
PATCH /api/bundles/<id>/ with new filter_unread and/or filter_shared values changes them, as a following GET shows, and leaves the other fields unchanged.
For a bundle, GET /api/bookmarks/?bundle=<id> returns only unread bookmarks matching the bundle when filter_unread is "yes", only read ones for "no", and both for "off".
For a bundle, GET /api/bookmarks/?bundle=<id> returns only shared bookmarks matching the bundle when filter_shared is "yes", only unshared for "no", and both for "off".
A bundle with a mix of filter_unread, filter_shared, search phrase and tag conditions returns only bookmarks that satisfy all conditions at once, via the API and via /bookmarks?bundle=<id>.

The /bundles/new and /bundles/<id>/edit forms show a "Reading State" dropdown (All, Unread, Read) and a "Sharing State" dropdown (All, Shared, Unshared); saving stores the choice, the edit form shows it preselected, and /bookmarks?bundle=<id> then lists only matching bookmarks. The "Found N bookmarks" preview follows the selected states.

ambiguities: Invalid values for filter_unread/filter_shared (e.g. "maybe", null, boolean true, uppercase "YES"): is the response 400, and with what error shape?
PUT on /api/bundles/<id>/ is in the contract but not in the criteria: does omitting the fields in a PUT reset them to "off" or keep the stored values?
PATCH omitting only one field: it is presumably left unchanged, but this is not stated.
Whether the bundle form dropdown defaults to "All" on /bundles/new, and what the edit form shows for existing bundles (assumed "All").
How the dropdown options map to values: All=off, Unread/Shared=yes, Read/Unshared=no is assumed; the form field names and option values are not given.
Whether the live preview on the form updates dynamically on dropdown change or only after saving or reloading. The ticket does not say.

How the bundle conditions interact with the bookmark list's own query parameters (q with `is:unread`, `is:shared`, or the unread/shared filter settings). For example, a bundle with filter_unread "yes" combined with a q of `!unread`.
Whether archived, deleted or other-user bookmarks are affected. Presumably unchanged, but this is not stated.
Whether the new fields apply to bookmark-list consumers other than the API and page (RSS feeds, bundle bookmark counts, the sidebar). The ticket names only the API and page.

Whether the bundles list page or the API list endpoint shows or paginates the new fields, and whether GET /api/bundles/ (list) includes them. The contract says GET, so the list is assumed to include them.
Behavior when the bundle has the `is:unread`-style terms in its own search phrase and also a filter_unread condition that conflicts.
structured.summary: Six criteria: four API-level (bundle create, bundle patch, and bookmark filtering by reading and sharing state), one combination criterion, and one browser form criterion. All are testable. The main unknowns are invalid-value handling, PUT semantics, form field names and defaults, and how the bundle conditions interact with the list's own filters.
